caption: What if you swam in Lake Natron? This shallow lake in northern Tanzania looks blood red, but the colour comes from salt-loving microbes with a red pigment. The water is no spa: its pH is 10 and higher, enough to burn skin and eyes, and it is often above 40 °C, reaching up to 60 °C in spots. Its salt, natron, is the same mineral ancient Egyptians used to dry out mummies. Yet about 2.5 million lesser flamingos live here, and 75% of the world's lesser flamingos are born here, nesting on salt islands where the caustic water keeps predators away. Plot twist: those viral photos of animals 'turned to stone'? The photographer placed them in living poses himself. The lake slowly preserves birds that had already died. Lesser flamingos live in India too, breeding in Gujarat, and every winter big flocks turn Mumbai's creeks pink. Would YOU visit Lake Natron? 👇
